title: Claude managed plugin scope decides over every other scope and is never updated (ADR Amendment 6, ruling 28)
description: opum-doc ADR distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md, Amendment 6, ruling 28 (ODOC-286, opum-doc commit 44326c5, opum-ai/opum-doc#458, on main 7818aca), read directly at 7818aca. The order becomes managed > local > project > user > synced. Ruling 28 supersedes ruling 26(ii) for managed only: managed is administrator policy the user cannot override, so a lower scope must never be reported as the one that decides. A managed deciding row is NEVER updated: no --scope managed update runs, the state is reported with scope: managed, and the remedy names the administrator managed settings instead of a command the user can run. That holds for the installed remedy, the disabled enable remedy, and agents --update-instructions, which must report update not-run. The amendment Disposition names QCLI-371 (merged 30a6846) as ranking managed below user; today claudeScopePrecedence in src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts is [local, project, user, managed, synced]. MEASUREMENT LIMIT, as the amendment records: no managed row has been observed from a real claude plugin list; the schema is read from the Claude Code 2.1.283 binary, where the install-scope enum includes managed and user and managed rows apply to every project. lore-cli owes the same ruling, so the managed remedy string must be agreed with lore-cli under ruling (d). Touches the same decoder as QCLI-379 (the within-scope depth tie-break): land that first or rebase onto it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: claude rows rank managed > local > project > user > synced: an applicable managed row decides over an enabled or disabled row of any other scope, in either list order
A managed deciding row is reported with scope managed, its remedy names the administrator managed settings (the text agreed with lore-cli), and no remedy or argv ever carries --scope managed
agents --update-instructions --target claude with a managed deciding row runs nothing beyond the list and reports update not-run, proven by a fake runtime that logs every call
Cited against opum-doc Amendment 6 (44326c5), with parity checked against lore-cli implementing commit; bun run check exits 0

plan: 1. claudeScopePrecedence becomes [managed, local, project, user, synced]; a managed row is never dropped for its projectPath (applies everywhere).

2. managedScopeRemedy (the agreed string) for installed and disabled managed rows; updateQuestPlugin reports not-run for an installed managed row with the agreed updateDetail; no --scope managed ever built.
3. test/qcli381-claude-managed-scope.test.ts over a logging fake claude, both list orders; mutation-check against the pre-change source.
4. AC4 parity: lore-cli has not landed LCLI-604 yet, so parity against its implementing commit is checked when it lands; the task stays open until then.
implementationNotes: REMEDY TEXT AGREED with lore-cli 2026-09-26 under ruling (d); opum-agent ruled that an agreed string binds without coming back. For quest, whenever the deciding Claude row has scope managed, in installed or disabled state alike, the remedy is exactly: managed by your Claude Code administrator: opum-quest@opum is set in the managed settings, which only an administrator can change. lore uses the same with opum-lore@opum, tracked as LCLI-604. Also agreed: the state keeps its value; scope managed is reported; --scope managed never appears in a remedy or argv; the manual update runs only the list and reports update not-run with that remedy. Order managed > local > project > user > synced; within one scope the deepest projectPath decides (ruling 29, QCLI-379); a managed row applies everywhere. One string for both states, and no OS path, both proposed by quest and agreed by lore.

SECOND STRING AGREED with lore-cli 2026-09-26 under ruling (d) (lore-cli reply, copied to opum-agent): on update not-run when the deciding claude row has scope managed and state installed, updateDetail is exactly "the deciding row is managed by your Claude Code administrator, so it is never updated" (no CLI name, no plugin id, so identical in both). A disabled managed row takes the existing disabled not-run path and still carries the managed remedy. Also agreed: a managed row is NOT filtered on projectPath in either CLI (lore today drops it at src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts:218; LCLI-604 exempts managed). IMPLEMENTED on branch fix/qcli-381-managed-scope-decides, stacked on #297 (QCLI-383), because the #297 merge is waiting on the user. EVIDENCE: 16 new cases pass; against the pre-change source 12 of 16 go red. The 4 green are the string pin, local over user, and managed over synced in both orders, which the old order [local, project, user, managed, synced] already satisfied. bun run check exit 0, 703 pass. AC4 is OPEN: lore-cli has no LCLI-604 implementing commit yet (origin/dev 6f6a527c records only the string), so parity against it cannot be checked.

TWO RULINGS FOLDED IN (opum-agent 2026-09-26, both from lore-cli review of LCLI-604). (1) Disabled wins among managed rows: with two or more applicable managed rows, any disabled one decides, in either list order; this changes only the reported state. decodeClaude now prefers a disabled managed row at equal rank. (2) LCLI-608: a managed deciding row carries the managed updateDetail when installed OR disabled, never the ordinary disabled detail, and no managed detail mentions enabling or a runnable update. updateQuestPlugin checks managed FIRST, ahead of the state and bare-call branches, so the detail QCLI-384 adds to the bare and disabled paths cannot reach a managed row. (A bare call resolves to codex and never reaches a claude row today; the ordering is defensive.) EVIDENCE: 19 cases pass. Two targeted mutations each turned exactly the predicted single case red: M1, dropping the disabled-wins clause, reddened only the enabled-first order, because first-listed already won in the other order; M2, limiting the managed detail to installed, reddened only the disabled-managed detail case. bun run check exit 0, 706 pass. Rebased onto origin/dev a82f835 after #297 merged. AC4 still OPEN pending the lore-cli LCLI-604 implementing commit.

AC4 PARITY READ against lore-cli e6d504f6 (LCLI-604 implementing commit 16e45330, #305, plus LCLI-608 e6d504f6, #308), read by SHA from the lore-cli object store. MATCHES: precedence [managed, local, project, user, synced] (lore src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts:194); managed exempt from the projectPath filter (:254); managed rows get depth zero and disabled wins among them in either order (decidesOver :211); MANAGED_SCOPE_REMEDY (core :158) and MANAGED_SCOPE_UPDATE_DETAIL (core :165) byte-identical modulo the plugin id; the managed detail applies to installed OR disabled and is checked ahead of the bare-call and disabled details (core :318); the managed update steps are empty (core :187), and quest reaches the same result by never calling port.update. ONE DIVERGENCE FOUND AND FIXED HERE: lore ranks printable(row.scope) (:250), so a padded "managed " decides first; quest ranked the raw string, which put it below synced while the report still treated it as managed. printable now lives in src/domain/agent-plugins.ts (adapters may import only domain and ports), re-exported from application, and the decoder ranks the printable form. Four new cases (managed-space and space-managed-BEL, both orders): reverting only that expression turns exactly those 4 red. bun run check exit 0, 710 pass. Cited against opum-doc ADR Amendment 6 (44326c5).
finalSummary: Ruling 28 (opum-doc ADR Amendment 6, 44326c5) in quest agents: Claude scopes rank managed > local > project > user > synced, a managed row applies to every project, and a disabled managed row wins among managed rows. A managed deciding row keeps its state, reports scope managed, and carries, in both states, the remedy and the not-run updateDetail agreed with lore-cli under ruling (d). It is never updated: only the list runs, and no --scope managed reaches a remedy or an argv. Landed in #298, plus a parity fix found by reading lore-cli e6d504f6: the decoder now ranks the scope in printable form, so a padded "managed " decides first as lore does. Verified with a call-logging fake claude in both list orders; mutations each reddened exactly the predicted cases (12/16 on the pre-change source; 1 each for the disabled-wins and managed-detail rulings; 4 for the padded scope); bun run check exit 0, 710 pass.
